people.name: Muhammad bin Qasim
people.summary: Arab general of the Umayyad caliphate who conquered Sind (712 CE) by defeating King Dahir.
facts: Defeated Dahir at Aror/Raor (712).
Introduced jizya on non-Muslims in Sind.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gopala I
people.summary: Founder of the Pala dynasty of Bengal (c. 750 CE), elected by chiefs to end anarchy (matsyanyaya).
facts: Chosen by the leading men to end "matsyanyaya" (rule of the big fish eating the small).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dharmapala
people.summary: Pala king of Bengal who founded the Vikramashila university and fought for Kanauj in the tripartite struggle.
facts: Founded Vikramashila (Bihar).
Placed his nominee Chakrayudha on the Kanauj throne.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nagabhata II
people.summary: Gurjara-Pratihara king who captured Kanauj (c. 816 CE), making it the Pratihara capital.
facts: Defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dantidurga
people.summary: Founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty (c. 753 CE), who overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami (NCERT).
facts: Performed the hiranyagarbha ritual to become a Kshatriya (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Krishna I
people.summary: Rashtrakuta king who built the rock-cut Kailasanatha temple at Ellora.
facts: Kailasa temple carved out of a single rock.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: E Hultzsch (Eugen Julius Theodor Hultzsch) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Amoghavarsha I
people.summary: Rashtrakuta king (814–878) who wrote the Kavirajamarga, the earliest Kannada work on poetics; capital Manyakheta.
facts: Patron of the Jaina scholar Jinasena.
Arab merchant Sulaiman called him one of the four great kings of the world.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Adi Shankaracharya
people.summary: Philosopher from Kaladi, Kerala, who taught Advaita (non-dualism) and set up four mathas (NCERT).
facts: Taught that the individual soul and the Supreme God are one (Advaita) (NCERT).
Founded mathas at Sringeri, Puri, Dwarka and Badrinath (Joshimath).
Wrote commentaries on the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras and Gita.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Rajaraja I
people.summary: Chola king (985–1014) who built the Brihadeshvara temple at Thanjavur and conquered northern Sri Lanka and the Maldives (NCERT).
facts: Built the Rajarajeshvara (Brihadeshvara) temple, Thanjavur (1010) (NCERT).
Organised a strong navy.
Married his daughter Kundavai to the Eastern Chalukya Vimaladitya.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

images.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Venu62~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Rajendra I
people.summary: Chola king (1014–1044) who led expeditions to the Ganga valley, Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia (Srivijaya) and built Gangaikondacholapuram (NCERT).
facts: Took the title Gangaikonda Chola after reaching the Ganga (NCERT).
Naval expedition to Srivijaya (Malaya, Sumatra) (1025).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Mahmud of Ghazni
people.summary: Sultan of Ghazni (Afghanistan) who raided the subcontinent 17 times between 1000 and 1025 (NCERT), including the Somnath temple.
facts: Raided 17 times (1000–1025) (NCERT).
Plundered Somnath (1025) (NCERT).
Took Al-Biruni to Ghazni (NCERT).
Ferdowsi wrote the Shahnama at his court.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Al-Biruni
people.summary: Scholar from Khwarizm brought to Ghazni by Mahmud (1017), who wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic about Indian society and science (NCERT).
facts: Born in Khwarizm (Uzbekistan) in 973 (NCERT).
Learnt Sanskrit and translated Indian works (NCERT).
Kitab-ul-Hind has 80 chapters on religion, philosophy, festivals, astronomy, social life (NCERT).
Saw barriers to understanding: language, religion, and the insularity of the locals (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 5 "Through the Eyes of Travellers"

images.credit: The original uploader was Romanm at Slovenian Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Rajaraja Narendra
people.summary: Eastern Chalukya king of Vengi at Rajahmundry who asked Nannaya to translate the Mahabharata into Telugu.
facts: Son of Vimaladitya and the Chola princess Kundavai; married Rajendra I's daughter Ammangadevi.
Capital Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nannaya
people.summary: "Adikavi" (first poet) of Telugu, who began the Andhra Mahabharatam at Rajaraja Narendra's court and wrote the first Telugu grammar, Andhra Shabda Chintamani.
facts: Translated the first two and a half parvas of the Mahabharata.
One of the Kavitrayam (Nannaya, Tikkana, Errana).
Helped by Narayana Bhatta.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kulottunga I
people.summary: Eastern Chalukya prince (Rajendra II) who became Chola emperor (1070), uniting Vengi and the Chola kingdom — the Chalukya-Chola line.
facts: Abolished tolls (Sungam Tavirtta Chola).
Sent an embassy of 72 merchants to China (1077).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ramanuja
people.summary: Philosopher from Sriperumbudur, inspired by the Alvars, who taught Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism) (NCERT).
facts: Taught that the soul, even when united with God, remains distinct (NCERT).
Worked at Srirangam; fled Chola persecution to the Hoysala court.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Basavanna
people.summary: Minister of the Kalachuri king Bijjala who founded the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement in Karnataka (NCERT).
facts: Challenged caste and ritual; wrote vachanas in Kannada (NCERT).
Anubhava Mantapa at Kalyani.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"

people.name: Brahma Naidu
people.summary: Minister of the Haihaya king Malideva who led his side in the Battle of Palnadu (Karempudi, c. 1182).
facts: Preached equality; held cosmopolitan dining (chapa kudu).
Hero of Srinatha's Palnati Viracharitra.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nayakuralu Nagamma
people.summary: Minister of King Nalagama who led his side against Brahma Naidu in the Battle of Palnadu (c. 1182); often called the first woman minister in Andhra.
facts: Won a cockfight wager that sent Malideva into exile.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Prithviraj Chauhan
people.summary: Chahamana (Chauhan) king of Delhi and Ajmer (1168–1192) who defeated Muhammad Ghori in 1191 but lost to him in 1192 (NCERT).
facts: Won the First Battle of Tarain (1191) (NCERT).
Lost the Second Battle of Tarain (1192) (NCERT).
Chand Bardai's Prithviraj Raso tells his story.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Muhammad Ghori
people.summary: Ruler of Ghor (Afghanistan) who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at Tarain (1192) (NCERT) and laid the base of Turkish rule in India.
facts: Lost the First Battle of Tarain (1191) and won the Second (1192) (NCERT).
Defeated Jaichand of Kanauj at Chandawar (1194).
Left Qutbuddin Aibak in charge in India.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Qutbuddin Aibak
people.summary: Turkish slave-general of Ghori who became the first Sultan of Delhi (1206–1210) (NCERT); began the Qutb Minar.
facts: Founded the Mamluk ("Slave") dynasty (NCERT: Qutbuddin Aybak 1206–1210).
Began the Qutb Minar and the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
Called Lakh Bakhsh (giver of lakhs).
Died in a polo accident at Lahore.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji
people.summary: Turkish general of Ghori who raided Bihar and Bengal and destroyed Nalanda and Vikramashila (c. 1193–1203).
facts: Captured Nadia from Lakshmana Sena (1204).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Iltutmish
people.summary: Sultan of Delhi (1211–1236) who consolidated the Sultanate, got the Caliph's recognition, introduced silver tanka and copper jital, and named his daughter Raziyya heir (NCERT).
facts: Formed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (group of forty) nobles.
Started the iqta system on a large scale.
Completed the Qutb Minar.
Saved the Sultanate from the Mongols by refusing refuge to Jalaluddin Mangbarni (1221).

roles.title: Sultan of Delhi
roles.howGained: Aibak's son-in-law; chosen by the nobles

people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Raziyya
people.summary: Daughter of Iltutmish who became Sultan in 1236 and was removed in 1240 (NCERT) — the only woman to rule from Delhi in the Sultanate.
facts: Minhaj-i Siraj recorded that nobles did not accept a woman ruler (NCERT).
Promoted the Abyssinian Yaqut.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Balban
people.summary: Sultan of Delhi (1266–1287) who broke the power of the Forty, introduced sijda and paibos, and held the theory of divine kingship (zil-i-ilahi).
facts: Destroyed the Chahalgani.
Set up the military department (diwan-i-arz).
Fought the Mongols.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Alauddin Khalji
people.summary: Sultan of Delhi (1296–1316) who repelled the Mongols, fixed market prices and sent Malik Kafur to raid the south (NCERT).
facts: Market reforms: fixed prices in Delhi (NCERT).
Paid soldiers in cash; branding of horses (dagh) and descriptive rolls (chehra).
Built Siri fort (NCERT).
Malik Kafur raided Warangal (1309), Devagiri and Madurai.
Measured land and collected half the produce as tax.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Malik Kafur
people.summary: Alauddin Khalji's general who led raids on Devagiri, Warangal (1309–10), Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
facts: Forced Prataparudra of Warangal to pay tribute (1310).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Amir Khusrau
people.summary: Poet and musician, disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, called the "Parrot of India"; served several Sultans (NCERT).
facts: Wrote in Persian and Hindavi; credited with qawwali and new ragas.
Wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh on Alauddin's campaigns.
Said in 1318 that every region had its own language (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

images.credit: Anonymous artist from Bokhara / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Nizamuddin Auliya
people.summary: Chishti Sufi saint of Delhi whose dargah draws pilgrims of all faiths (NCERT).
facts: Disciple of Baba Farid; teacher of Amir Khusrau (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"

people.name: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
people.summary: Founder of the Tughlaq dynasty (1320–1325); built Tughlaqabad; his son Ulugh Khan conquered Warangal (1323).
facts: Died when a pavilion collapsed (1325).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Muhammad bin Tughlaq
people.summary: Sultan of Delhi (1325–1351) known for bold experiments: moving the capital to Daulatabad, token currency and the Khurasan plan (NCERT); as Ulugh Khan he took Warangal (1323).
facts: Moved people from Delhi to Daulatabad (1327) (NCERT).
Introduced token copper currency (NCERT).
Raised a huge army for Khurasan (NCERT).
Ibn Battuta served as qazi of Delhi under him (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Prola II
people.summary: Kakatiya chief who began to break away from the Kalyani Chalukyas; father of Rudradeva.
facts: Ruled from Anumakonda (Hanamkonda).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rudradeva
people.summary: Kakatiya king (Prataparudra I) who declared independence (c. 1163) and built the Thousand Pillar temple at Hanamkonda.
facts: Anumakonda inscription (1163).
Began building Warangal fort.
Wrote Nitisara.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ganapati Deva
people.summary: Greatest Kakatiya king (1199–1262), who moved the capital to Warangal (Orugallu), built tanks and promoted trade at Motupalli.
facts: Built Pakhala, Ramappa and Laknavaram lakes (by his chiefs); Ramappa temple built by his general Recharla Rudra (1213).
Motupalli abhaya-shasana protected sea traders.
Had no son; named his daughter Rudrama his heir.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Skorthiw at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Rudramadevi
people.summary: Kakatiya queen of Warangal (1262–1289) (NCERT) who ruled in her own name as "Rudradeva Maharaja"; praised by Marco Polo.
facts: NCERT contrasts her with Raziyya: she changed her name on inscriptions and pretended to be a man (NCERT).
Defeated the Yadavas of Devagiri.
Marco Polo praised her rule (1293).
Killed fighting Kayastha chief Ambadeva (c. 1289).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Prataparudra II
people.summary: Last Kakatiya king (1289–1323), who paid tribute to Malik Kafur (1310) and was defeated by Ulugh Khan (1323); died on the way to Delhi.
facts: His defeat ended the Kakatiyas (1323).
Under him the 77 Nayakas (Nayankara system, begun earlier) commanded the forts.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tikkana
people.summary: Telugu poet at the Nellore court of Manumasiddhi who translated 15 parvas of the Mahabharata; called "Kavi Brahma".
facts: Second of the Kavitrayam.
Also wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Marco Polo
people.summary: Venetian traveller who visited Motupalli, the Kakatiya port, around 1293 and praised Rudramadevi's rule and Golconda's diamonds.
facts: Visited Kayal, Malabar and the Kakatiya kingdom on his way back from China.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Genghis Khan
people.summary: Mongol ruler whose invasion of Transoxiana (1219) threatened the Delhi Sultanate (NCERT); the Mughals descended from him through their mothers.
facts: Chased Jalaluddin Mangbarni to the Indus (1221).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Ibn Battuta
people.summary: Moroccan traveller who reached Sind in 1333, served Muhammad bin Tughlaq as qazi of Delhi and wrote the Rihla (NCERT).
facts: Reached Sind in 1333 (NCERT).
Sent as envoy to China in 1342 (NCERT).
Described the coconut, the paan, Indian cities and the postal system (NCERT).
Returned home in 1354 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 5 "Through the Eyes of Travellers"

people.name: Firoz Shah Tughlaq
people.summary: Sultan of Delhi (1351–1388) who built canals and towns, imposed jizya on brahmanas, and moved two Ashokan pillars to Delhi.
facts: Built canals from the Yamuna and Sutlej.
Founded Firozabad, Jaunpur and Hisar.
Moved Ashokan pillars from Topra and Meerut to Delhi.
Wrote Futuhat-i-Firozshahi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Amir Timur
people.summary: Central Asian conqueror who sacked Delhi in 1398; the Mughals descended from him on their father's side (NCERT).
facts: Sacked Delhi (December 1398).
Babur was his descendant (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Bahlul Lodi
people.summary: Afghan founder of the Lodi dynasty (1451–1489), the first Afghan dynasty of Delhi.
facts: Conquered the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sikandar Lodi
people.summary: Lodi Sultan (1489–1517) who founded Agra (1504) and introduced the gaz-i-Sikandari measure.
facts: Founded Agra as his capital (1504).
Wrote Persian verse under the name Gulrukhi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ibrahim Lodi
people.summary: Last Sultan of Delhi (1517–1526), killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat.
facts: Angered his nobles; Daulat Khan Lodi invited Babur.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Harihara I
people.summary: Co-founder with his brother Bukka of the Vijayanagara empire (1336) (NCERT); first ruler of the Sangama dynasty.
facts: Founded Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra (NCERT).
Guided by the sage Vidyaranya, by tradition.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

people.name: Bukka Raya I
people.summary: Co-founder of Vijayanagara with his brother Harihara (1336) (NCERT); his son Kumara Kampana took Madurai.
facts: Sent an embassy to China.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

people.name: Vidyaranya
people.summary: Head of the Sringeri matha who, by tradition, inspired Harihara and Bukka to found Vijayanagara.
facts: Wrote Panchadashi.
Brother of Sayana, the Vedic commentator.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: This plate is contained in the book “Vijayanagara Paintings” / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
people.summary: Telugu chief who led the revolt that freed coastal Andhra and Telangana from the Tughlaqs (c. 1326–1333); Vilasa grant.
facts: His Vilasa grant describes Tughlaq oppression and the liberation.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka
people.summary: Cousin of Prolaya Nayaka who captured Warangal (1336) and helped found the Bahmani kingdom (1347).
facts: Ruled from Warangal; later lost it to the Bahmanis and Recherla Velamas (1368).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Prolaya Vema Reddi
people.summary: Founder of the Reddi kingdom of Addanki (c. 1325), patron of the poet Errana.
facts: Restored agraharas and temples after the Tughlaq conquest.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Errana
people.summary: Telugu poet at Prolaya Vema Reddi's court who completed the Andhra Mahabharatam; third of the Kavitrayam.
facts: Completed the remaining Aranya parva.
Wrote Harivamsam.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Srinatha
people.summary: Telugu poet, "Vidyadhikari" at the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddi of Kondavidu; wrote Sringara Naishadhamu and Palnati Viracharitra.
facts: Defeated Dindima Bhatta in debate at Deva Raya II's court; honoured with a bath of gold coins (kanakabhishekam).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah
people.summary: Founder of the Bahmani sultanate (1347) with capital Gulbarga, after revolting against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
facts: Also called Hasan Gangu.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mahmud Gawan
people.summary: Persian-born prime minister of the Bahmani sultanate who built a great madrasa at Bidar and was executed in 1481.
facts: Reformed revenue and divided provinces.
Executed on false charges (1481); the kingdom then broke up.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Deva Raya II
people.summary: Sangama king of Vijayanagara (1424–1446) who employed Muslim cavalry and archers; Abdur Razzaq visited his court.
facts: Patron of Srinatha (by tradition).
Called "Gajabetekara" (hunter of elephants).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Abdur Razzaq
people.summary: Persian ambassador from Herat who visited Vijayanagara in 1443 and described its seven walls (NCERT).
facts: Described the city as without equal in the world (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

people.name: Guru Nanak
people.summary: Founder of Sikhism, born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib), who taught devotion to one formless God and set up a community at Kartarpur (NCERT).
facts: Rejected sacrifices, ritual baths and caste; taught nam, dan and isnan (NCERT).
Langar (common kitchen) at Kartarpur (NCERT).
Appointed Angad as successor (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"

images.credit: Amritpal Singh Mann. Painted by Jaimal Singh Naqqash (1860–1916), Mehtab Singh Naqqash (1871–1940), and Hukum Singh. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Kabir
people.summary: Bhakti poet-saint of Benares who rejected both Hindu and Muslim ritual and worshipped a formless God (NCERT).
facts: His verses are in the Bijak, the Kabir Granthavali and the Guru Granth Sahib (NCERT).
A weaver by tradition (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"

people.name: Tallapaka Annamacharya
people.summary: Telugu saint-composer of Tirumala who wrote about 32,000 kirtanas on Lord Venkateswara; "Pada Kavita Pitamaha".
facts: Born at Tallapaka, Kadapa district.
His songs were inscribed on copper plates at Tirumala.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bammera Potana
people.summary: Telugu poet who translated the Bhagavata Purana as the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu and refused to dedicate it to a king.
facts: From Bammera near Warangal.
Dedicated his work to Lord Rama.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vasco da Gama
people.summary: Portuguese navigator who reached Calicut on 20 May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India round Africa.
facts: Received by the Zamorin of Calicut.
Guided across the Arabian Sea by a Gujarati pilot.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Afonso de Albuquerque
people.summary: Portuguese governor who captured Goa from the Bijapur sultan (1510), the real founder of Portuguese power in India.
facts: Encouraged Portuguese men to marry Indian women.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Krishnadevaraya
people.summary: Greatest Tuluva king of Vijayanagara (1509–1529) (NCERT): took the Raichur doab, subdued Odisha and wrote the Telugu poem Amuktamalyada.
facts: Acquired the Raichur doab (1512), subdued Orissa (1514) and defeated Bijapur (1520) (NCERT).
Wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu (NCERT).
Eight poets (Ashtadiggajas) at his court; Allasani Peddana the chief.
Built the Vitthala and Hazara Rama temples and the gopurams (NCERT).
Visited Tirumala seven times.
Titles: Andhra Bhoja, Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

images.credit: Ravitheja Kumar Reddy C / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Allasani Peddana
people.summary: Chief of the Ashtadiggajas at Krishnadevaraya's court; wrote Manucharitra; "Andhra Kavita Pitamaha".
facts: Krishnadevaraya is said to have carried his palanquin.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tenali Ramakrishna
people.summary: Witty poet of Krishnadevaraya's court (Ashtadiggaja) who wrote Panduranga Mahatmyam.
facts: Famous for folk tales of his wit.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Domingo Paes
people.summary: Portuguese traveller who described Vijayanagara under Krishnadevaraya (c. 1520) (NCERT).
facts: Described the Mahanavami festival and the king (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

people.name: Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk
people.summary: Bahmani governor of Telangana who founded the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda (1518).
facts: Murdered at prayer by his son Jamsheed (1543).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ibrahim Qutb Shah
people.summary: Qutb Shahi sultan (1550–1580) who lived at Vijayanagara in exile and patronised Telugu poets, who called him "Malki Bharama".
facts: Joined the alliance that defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565).
Built Hussain Sagar (1562).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
people.summary: Qutb Shahi sultan (1580–1612) who founded Hyderabad (1591) and built the Charminar; a poet in Dakhni Urdu.
facts: First "sahib-e-diwan" poet of Urdu.
Legend links Hyderabad's old name Bhagyanagar to Bhagmati.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Ali Riza (The Bodleian Painter) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Aliya Rama Raya
people.summary: Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and Vijayanagara regent who was defeated and killed at Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota), 1565 (NCERT).
facts: Played the Deccan sultanates against each other (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 7 "An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara"

people.name: Babur
people.summary: Founder of the Mughal empire who won the First Battle of Panipat (1526) and wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama (NCERT).
facts: Descended from Timur and Genghis Khan (NCERT).
Seized Kabul in 1504 (NCERT).
Used guns and the tulughma tactic.
Wrote the Baburnama in Turkish.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Rana Sanga
people.summary: Rajput ruler of Mewar defeated by Babur at Khanwa (1527).
facts: Led a Rajput confederacy.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Humayun
people.summary: Second Mughal emperor, defeated by Sher Shah (Chausa 1539, Kanauj 1540), who fled to Iran and regained Delhi in 1555 (NCERT).
facts: Took refuge with the Safavid Shah of Iran (NCERT).
Died falling from the steps of his library (1556).
His sister Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Sher Shah Suri
people.summary: Afghan ruler who defeated Humayun (1539, 1540) and ruled Delhi (1540–1545) (NCERT); known for the rupia, roads and land survey.
facts: Introduced the silver rupiya.
Rebuilt the Grand Trunk Road with sarais.
Measured land; his revenue system was the basis of Akbar's (NCERT says his administration was taken up by Akbar).
Died in an explosion at Kalinjar (1545).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Hemu
people.summary: Minister and general of the Sur ruler Adil Shah who took Delhi and was defeated at the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).
facts: Took the title Vikramaditya on capturing Delhi.
Wounded by an arrow in the eye; captured and killed.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bairam Khan
people.summary: Akbar's guardian and regent who won the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).
facts: Regent 1556–1560; dismissed in 1560; killed on the way to Mecca.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Akbar
people.summary: Greatest Mughal emperor (1556–1605) (NCERT): built the empire, the mansab and zabt systems, and the policy of sulh-i kul (universal peace).
facts: Crowned at Kalanaur aged 13 (1556).
Built Fatehpur Sikri and the Ibadat Khana (1575) (NCERT).
Abolished the pilgrim tax (1563) and jizya (1564).
Mansabdari system and Todar Mal's zabt revenue system (NCERT).
Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama (NCERT).

roles.title: Mughal emperor
roles.howGained: Succeeded his father under Bairam Khan's regency

people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Maharana Pratap
people.summary: Ruler of Mewar from 1572 (NCERT) who refused to accept Mughal rule and fought at Haldighati (1576).
facts: Fought Man Singh at Haldighati (1576).
His horse Chetak is famous.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Raja Man Singh
people.summary: Kachhwaha Rajput of Amber who led Akbar's army at Haldighati (1576) and was one of his top mansabdars.
facts: Governor of Kabul, Bihar and Bengal.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Abul Fazl
people.summary: Akbar's friend and historian who wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i Akbari (NCERT).
facts: Ain-i Akbari describes administration, revenue and society (NCERT).
Killed by Bir Singh Bundela on Prince Salim's orders (1602).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 9 "Kings and Chronicles: The Mughal Courts"

people.name: Todar Mal
people.summary: Akbar's revenue minister who carried out a careful survey of crop yields and prices — the zabt system (NCERT).
facts: Earlier served Sher Shah.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Jahangir
people.summary: Mughal emperor (1605–1627) who married Nur Jahan (1611) (NCERT), received Sir Thomas Roe and set up the chain of justice.
facts: Prince Salim; wrote the Tuzuk-i Jahangiri.
Executed Guru Arjan Dev (1606).
Gave the English permission to trade at Surat (1613).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Nur Jahan
people.summary: Mehrunnisa, who married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Nur Jahan (NCERT); she issued coins and orders in her name.
facts: Her name appeared on coins (NCERT).
Her family (Itimad-ud-Daula, Asaf Khan) dominated the court.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Thomas Roe
people.summary: English ambassador of James I to Jahangir's court (1615–1619) who won trading rights for the East India Company.
facts: Earlier William Hawkins had visited Jahangir (1609).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: After Michiel Jansz. van Mierevelt / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Shah Jahan
people.summary: Mughal emperor (1628–1658) who built the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad, and was imprisoned by his son Aurangzeb (NCERT).
facts: Built the Taj Mahal for Mumtaz Mahal (NCERT).
Built the Red Fort and Jama Masjid of Delhi (NCERT).
Peacock Throne.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Francois Bernier
people.summary: French doctor in India (1656–1668) who compared Mughal India unfavourably with Europe and claimed there was no private property in land (NCERT).
facts: Physician to Prince Dara Shukoh (NCERT).
Wrote Travels in the Mogul Empire (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 5 "Through the Eyes of Travellers"

people.name: Dara Shukoh
people.summary: Shah Jahan's eldest son, a scholar who translated the Upanishads into Persian; defeated by Aurangzeb at Samugarh (1658) and executed.
facts: Wrote Majma-ul-Bahrain (the meeting of two oceans).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Aurangzeb
people.summary: Mughal emperor (1658–1707) under whom the empire reached its largest size and who spent 25 years fighting in the Deccan (NCERT).
facts: Won the war of succession (Samugarh, 1658).
Reimposed jizya (1679).
Annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687).
Died at Ahmednagar (1707) (NCERT).

roles.title: Mughal emperor
roles.howGained: Defeated his brothers and imprisoned his father

people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

images.credit: Darbarscene.jpg: Cordanrad derivative work: Rani nurmai (talk) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Shivaji
people.summary: Founder of the Maratha kingdom (1674 coronation), born at Shivneri to Shahji and Jija Bai (NCERT).
facts: Built a kingdom with the support of deshmukhs (NCERT).
Escaped from Agra (1666).
Crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad (1674).
Chauth and sardeshmukhi; Ashtapradhan council.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Mirza Raja Jai Singh
people.summary: Mughal general of Amber who forced Shivaji to sign the Treaty of Purandar (1665).
facts: Sent Shivaji to Aurangzeb's court at Agra (1666).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Guru Tegh Bahadur
people.summary: Ninth Sikh Guru, executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi (1675).
facts: Gurdwara Sis Ganj marks the place.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Guru Gobind Singh
people.summary: Tenth Sikh Guru who founded the Khalsa in 1699 (NCERT) and declared the Granth Sahib the eternal Guru.
facts: Fought Rajput and Mughal rulers (NCERT).
Compiled the Dasam Granth.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah
people.summary: Last Qutb Shahi sultan (Tana Shah, 1672–1687), whose ministers were Madanna and Akkanna; lost Golconda to Aurangzeb (1687).
facts: Imprisoned at Daulatabad till death.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Madanna
people.summary: Brahmin chief minister of Tana Shah who, with his brother Akkanna, ran Golconda; both were killed in 1686.
facts: Nephew of Kancherla Gopanna (Ramadasu).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bhakta Ramadasu
people.summary: Kancherla Gopanna, tahsildar of Bhadrachalam under Tana Shah, who built the Rama temple there with revenue money and was jailed; composer of Rama kirtanas.
facts: Imprisoned at Golconda for 12 years, by tradition.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Banda Bahadur
people.summary: Sikh leader who set up his own administration and coins after Guru Gobind Singh; captured in 1715 and executed in 1716 (NCERT).
facts: Struck coins in the name of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Baji Rao I
people.summary: Peshwa (1720–1740) who expanded Maratha power north to Malwa and raided Delhi (1737) (NCERT).
facts: Defeated Nizam-ul-Mulk at Palkhed (1728) and Bhopal (1738).
Never lost a battle, by tradition.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I
people.summary: Mughal noble who became virtually independent in the Deccan after the Battle of Shakar Kheda (1724), founding the Asaf Jahi (Nizam) line of Hyderabad (NCERT).
facts: Held the subadari of the Deccan (NCERT).
Was briefly wazir of Muhammad Shah (1722).

roles.title: Nizam of Hyderabad
roles.howGained: Defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda

people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Nadir Shah
people.summary: Ruler of Iran who defeated the Mughals at Karnal and sacked Delhi in 1739 (NCERT), carrying away the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor.
facts: Battle of Karnal (February 1739).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Muhammad Shah
people.summary: Mughal emperor (1719–1748) during whose reign the Nizam, Awadh and Bengal became virtually independent and Nadir Shah sacked Delhi.
facts: Called "Rangila".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Murshid Quli Khan
people.summary: Founder of the autonomous Nawabs of Bengal; deputy governor (naib) under Aurangzeb and subadar from 1717 (NCERT).
facts: Moved the capital to Murshidabad.
Collected revenue through ijaradars.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

images.credit: W. H. Allen and Co. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Burhan-ul-Mulk Saadat Khan
people.summary: Founder of the autonomous state of Awadh (subadar from 1722) (NCERT).
facts: Held the offices of subadari, diwani and faujdari (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II

people.name: Joseph-Francois Dupleix
people.summary: French governor-general at Pondicherry (1742–1754) who led French ambitions in the Carnatic Wars.
facts: Took Madras (1746); won at Adyar through Paradis.
Recalled to France (1754).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tailapa II
people.summary: Founder of the Chalukyas of Kalyani (Western Chalukyas, 973), who overthrew the last Rashtrakuta.
facts: Defeated and killed the Paramara king Munja.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vikramaditya VI
people.summary: Greatest Kalyani Chalukya king (1076–1126), who began the Chalukya-Vikrama era; Bilhana wrote his life and Vijnaneshwara the Mitakshara at his court.
facts: Fought the Cholas over Vengi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: B. Lewis Rice (Benjamin Lewis Rice, 1837-1927) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Kapilendra Deva
people.summary: Founder of the Suryavamshi Gajapati dynasty of Odisha (1435), who conquered coastal Andhra up to the Krishna and beyond, including Kondavidu and Rajahmundry.
facts: Founder of the Suryavamshi Gajapati dynasty of Odisha (1435), who conquered coastal Andhra up to the Krishna and beyond, including Kondavidu and Rajahmundry.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Prataparudra Deva
people.summary: Gajapati king of Odisha (1497–1540) who lost Kondavidu and the coastal Andhra lands to Krishnadevaraya and gave him his daughter in marriage; a follower of Chaitanya.
facts: Gajapati king of Odisha (1497–1540) who lost Kondavidu and the coastal Andhra lands to Krishnadevaraya and gave him his daughter in marriage; a follower of Chaitanya.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sarvajna Singabhupala
people.summary: Recherla Velama king of Rachakonda (14th–15th century) and scholar who wrote the Rasarnava Sudhakara on poetics; Potana is said to have refused to dedicate his work to him.
facts: Recherla Velama king of Rachakonda (14th–15th century) and scholar who wrote the Rasarnava Sudhakara on poetics; Potana is said to have refused to dedicate his work to him.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
